text: There would have been several media reports which suggest that more and more consumers are buying online.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, in the online transactions, consumers are all disadvantaged because of the lack of bargaining power in negotiating the standard terms and conditions of trade.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, we understand that it is common for low-cost carriers operating out of Singapore to use pre-ticked boxes when transacting with consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: A recent case in mind involving a premium carrier is that of Singapore Airlines (SIA) which had a pre-ticked box for auto inclusion of travel insurance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the EU, companies cannot infer consumer’s consent for additional payments by using such pre-ticked boxes and must obtain the express consent of consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I urge MTI to consider similar subsidiary legislation to the same effect.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Members for their comments and suggestions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked about the outlook for the global economy in 2018 and the implications for the Singapore economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We expect global economic growth to pick up slightly in 2018, partly on the back of improved growth prospects in the US due to the recently approved tax reforms.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: However, as compared to 2017, growth in most of Singapore’s key final demand markets, such as the Eurozone, China, the Newly Industrialising Economies and ASEAN-5, is projected to moderate or remain unchanged.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: At the same time, while global macroeconomic risks have receded to some extent since the end of 2017, there remain some downside risks to global growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: First, there remain concerns over protectionist actions, which could disrupt global trade and economic growth if they translate into trade barriers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Second, the US' economic recovery is in a relatively mature stage of the cycle.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: An upside surprise in inflation could lead to a faster-than-expected normalisation of US monetary policy, with consequent impact on the US and the global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Against this backdrop, Singapore’s economic growth is likely to moderate in 2018, but still remain firm.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We expect the performance of our sectors to vary.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The manufacturing sector, alongside externally-oriented services sectors, such as finance and insurance, transportation and storage, and wholesale trade, are likely to sustain growth due to firm external demand.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Growth is also expected to broaden to domestically-oriented services sectors like retail and food services as consumer sentiments improve in tandem with the ongoing recovery in the labour market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: However, the performance of the construction sector and the marine and offshore engineering industry is likely to remain lacklustre due to weak operating conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Innovation cycles have shortened, and new technologies are disrupting many sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Second, global value chains are changing, as major trading partners promote in-sourcing and move up the manufacturing value chain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In the US, the Trump administration has highlighted its plans to boost its manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: China has embarked on a "Made in China 2025" initiative, and India has its "Make in India" initiative, too.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Third, there is a shift in global economic weight towards Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We are witnessing the rise of China, India and Southeast Asia with a growing middle class, increased urbanisation, and infrastructure development efforts, such as the BRI.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: To strengthen our competitive edge, we must, therefore, continue to strengthen our linkages, innovate and deepen our capabilities to prevent being displaced by the global shifts that I mentioned just now.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Looking ahead, we recognise two major drivers of economic success – internationalisation and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about our trade priorities and whether our pursuit of FTAs is still relevant in the current global economic climate.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: As a small country with an open economy, connectivity is core to Singapore’s survival and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Having free and open markets is critical for Singapore’s development.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: It is by staying open to trade, people and ideas that we can participate in global growth and build the deep capabilities needed for our people and companies to access new markets, on-board cutting-edge technologies and create good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Singapore, therefore, remains committed to the multilateral and rules-based trading system.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: To illustrate with an example, plastics product manufacturer Singa Plastics Ltd has taken advantage of several of our FTAs, such as the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement, the ASEAN-Korea FTA, as well as the Singapore-Australia FTA, to grow its business and maintain competitive pricing for its exports into these countries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The company’s exports have increased by close to 30% since it began using these FTAs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: As Singa Plastics also exports to France, Germany and Greece, it is keenly awaiting the ratification of the EU-Singapore FTA (EUSFTA).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will continue to enhance our connectivity by strengthening connections with existing trading partners as well as forging new connections with emerging markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will continue to work with the European Commission to expedite the ratification of the EUSFTA.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We review our FTAs from time to time, and upgrade them to ensure that they remain relevant and useful to our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: There is, for example, the ongoing negotiations with China to review and upgrade the China-Singapore FTA.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The upgrade looks to deepen bilateral benefits by enhancing areas, such as investment provisions, trade facilitation, rules of origin, and improved market access for Singapore businesses, especially in the services sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We are expanding Singapore's connectivity by joining regional FTAs, such as CPTPP, which will be signed next week, and the ongoing Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Singapore is also negotiating FTAs with major regional blocs, such as the Eurasian Economic Union and the Pacific Alliance.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan observed that more should be done to promote the opportunities of CPTPP to our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Our pursuit of FTAs is for the benefit of our companies and their workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will continue to work with the Singapore Business Federation (SBF) and TACs on outreach efforts to help our companies, in particular, our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These efforts include company outreach sessions, FTA training courses, and even one-on-one sessions to follow up on specific concerns or opportunities which companies are keen on.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Ms Sun Xueling asked about the Government’s plans to help Singapore companies take advantage of the shift in global economic focus towards Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Indeed, Asia's growth brings about many opportunities, with rising consumption as well as demand for infrastructure in Asia offering significant export and investment opportunities for Singapore-based companies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We are working with China on commercially meaningful areas in its BRI.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: BRI has the potential to foster regional cooperation, enhance connectivity and accelerate infrastructure development across Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Singapore companies are well-placed to tap on BRI opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We are also collaborating with the Government of Andhra Pradesh in India to develop the state’s new capital city of Amaravati, as well as to promote greater economic collaboration with Andhra Pradesh.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In 2017, Ascendas-Singbridge and SembCorp Development formed a Singapore Consortium to master-develop the commercial core of Amaravati, together with its government.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Since then, our companies have been actively exploring smart city urban solution opportunities in Amaravati.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Closer to home, ASEAN has strong potential as a market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We are strengthening our engagements with ASEAN through both regional economic integration as well as bilateral initiatives with the ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sun Xueling asked about our plans to work with other ASEAN member states to unlock ASEAN's potential to benefit Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: As a region, ASEAN is making good progress in deepening economic integration under AEC.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: By 2030, ASEAN has the potential to become the fourth largest single market in the world after China, the US and the EU.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Despite the rising nationalistic tendencies and anti-trade sentiments elsewhere in the world, ASEAN has stayed on course in its trajectory of regional economic integration.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: ASEAN is also navigating the rapid pace of technological change and digital disruption.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: For businesses seeking to enter or expand their presence in ASEAN markets and beyond, AEC, since its realisation in 2015, has lowered entry barriers, reduced transaction costs, widened choices for consumers and generated job opportunities in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The company started out as a single home appliance shop in 1998.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Today, their products are carried by over 450 retailers in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: It has been using the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement since 2015 for its products to enjoy tariff savings and has experienced a close to 15% increase in exports since then.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Trends Home Electrical plans to continue innovating, upgrading its capabilities and further expand into Southeast Asia to capture the growth opportunities there.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: At this juncture, Mr Chairman, I would like to clarify on Mr Low Thia Khiang's comment that while AEC was established by the end of 2015, but ASEAN failed to achieve one-fifth of the 506 measures and had deferred them for 10 years to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: So, we are not deferring them to 2025.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: And, this year, as part of Singapore's ASEAN Chairmanship, we are pursuing an ASEAN agreement on e-commerce to help our businesses expand and leverage the e-commerce market potential in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The ASEAN e-commerce scene is still at its infancy, with some companies finding it confusing to navigate the varying e-commerce regulations in various ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This agreement that we are aiming to sign this year will streamline some of these regulations so that aspiring entrepreneurs and SMEs can market their products and services regionally with greater ease and make it safer to send and receive electronic payments.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: With this agreement, companies like Coldwear, a local winter wear and travel accessories retailer, can expect to use e-commerce solutions to expand into the ASEAN region more easily.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Coldwear has successfully entered the Indonesian market and plans to venture into the wider ASEAN markets, including the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Chairman, our strategy of engaging ASEAN will also take place at the bilateral level.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will press on with our suite of bilateral initiatives to deepen our economic linkages and help our companies take advantage of the opportunities in our neighbouring ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will intensify our engagements with our long-term partners, such as Malaysia and Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: New collaborations, such as the High Speed Rail and the Rapid Transit System will enhance bilateral connectivity, business links and people-to-people exchanges between Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: ESG will continue to explore areas of synergies in Indonesia.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Kendal Industrial Park in Central Java, a joint venture between SembCorp Development and an Indonesian company, is one example.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We hope to be able to facilitate more of such partnerships in future.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will also continue to extend our reach into other ASEAN countries, such as Myanmar and Vietnam, where our companies have strong and sustained interests.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Chairman, the second major driver of our economic success is innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: With shifting factors of production now favouring technology-intensive economies, Singapore’s focus on innovation and technology puts us in a position of strength to transform our installed base, capture new investments and create new solutions for the market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Our strengths in innovation and technology have been developed through consistent R&D efforts over the years, which have raised Singapore’s global competitiveness and enabled many of our sectors to move up the value chain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Beyond R&D, we are also making a strong, committed push towards building innovation networks and partnerships to link up companies across major innovation hubs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This is a reflection of the nature of innovation in a digital age, and the importance of cross-market perspectives for businesses to reap new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) was launched last year and seeks to strengthen Singapore’s connections to major innovation hubs around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: It creates more opportunities for our students, entrepreneurs and businesses to gain overseas experience, connect and collaborate with their overseas counterparts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The connections facilitated under GIA will allow ideas and talents to cross-fertilise across different innovation hubs and provide access to interact with and identify local partners for collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This injects vibrancy into our local innovation ecosystem and bolsters our value proposition as a springboard for foreign companies to come and testbed new ideas here before expanding into the region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: A key component of GIA is to create a network of Innovation Launchpads around the world.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We recognise that our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), companies and agencies have already established their own networks abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: GIA seeks to integrate them into a single network that companies can readily tap on to launch their innovations into the relevant markets.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: My colleagues will share further on the progress of our R&D efforts and GIA initiative later on.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We will also take advantage of our ASEAN Chairmanship to work on an ASEAN Innovation Network (AIN).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The intent is to strengthen the networks among the innovation ecosystems in ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This will further enable our companies to expand abroad and help them to better respond to demands from the increasingly sophisticated and growing consumer base in our region.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The ITMs are designed to keep our industries competitive and generate growth for Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Moving forward, we will continue to refine the ITMs, together with our partners, working closely with all stakeholders, including companies, TACs, unions and workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: My colleagues will also elaborate further on the progress of our ITMs and our restructuring efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about our strategy to help our companies remain competitive and support sustained growth, especially given our overheads and cost structure.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Along the same vein, Mr Leon Perera asked about the Government's approach to keeping industrial land costs competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Government monitors business costs closely to ensure that we remain competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: However, there were differences across the different sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The overall ULC is likely to see a modest increase this year.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Wages are expected to rise amidst a gradual recovery in the labour market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The key, therefore, for companies to manage their labour costs and have sustainable wage growth for Singaporeans, is to have continued productivity growth.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: For companies in the manufacturing sector, rental costs constitute a relatively small proportion of business costs, and are usually less than 2% on average.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We have, nonetheless, taken measures to ensure that industrial land costs remain competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: First of all, JTC Corporation benchmarks its land prices internationally to ensure that they are competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Second, the Government releases land for private-sector industrial developments through a half-yearly Industrial Government Land Sales Programme to ensure that there is sufficient land and industrial space to meet demand and to support our economic growth, as well as to maintain the stability of the industrial property market.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We must continue to take bold strides to seize opportunities to innovate and not let our domestic constraints of a tightening labour market and scarcity of land to hold us back.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Mr Chairman, we have put in place initiatives to ensure that our companies remain competitive and are well-poised to tap into growth areas and take up future challenges posed by the global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Coupled with the positive growth forecast in the year ahead, I would like to encourage our companies to take advantage of the firm global economic prospects to persevere on their transformation and growth journey.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We welcome companies to be actively engaged in our efforts as we work to expand Singapore's economic space through building and deepening linkages, and establishing innovation networks to foster relationships and create opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Chairman of the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Finance and Trade and Industry, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, and all Members for their comments and suggestions on our economic transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Aggregate data, like GDP growth, give us a feel for the overall economy and its direction, but they do not tell us the whole story, especially the unevenness in the economic terrain.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The pace and success of transformation vary according to the context of a particular sector or enterprise.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And this variation is due to different capabilities, external demand conditions and even different levels of aspiration.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our efforts to transform the economy must recognise this diversity of circumstances and needs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And our strategies must also be nimble and adapt with the times.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: That is why we are making changes to Government policies and programmes, and even to the way that we are organised.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to display some slides?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, our sectors face a spectrum of external demand conditions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: On the other hand, the real VA of the Transport Engineering cluster contracted by 12.2% pa over the same period, due to the fall in demand for the marine and offshore segment.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, between 2015 and 2017, the real VA of externally-oriented sectors grew by 3.6% pa, compared to 0.7% pa for domestically-oriented sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Third, even among the domestically-oriented sectors, their ability to reduce manpower-intensity and raise productivity has varied.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The real VA of retail trade and food services have grown over the past two years by 2.7% pa and 1.2% pa respectively.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: However, retail trade’s growth has been much more productivity-driven, with VA per worker rising at 3.3% pa, unlike the decline of 1.9% pa in food services.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Using VA per actual hour worked shows better productivity performance for both sectors, but an even wider gap between the two.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Given this variation, the ITMs aim to address each sector’s particular combination of challenges and circumstances.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, the ITMs' support our externally-oriented sectors’ growth and aspirations for market leadership, through the development of high-value capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To achieve this, the ITM advocates the development of specialised logistics handling capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If I can illustrate, Tee Hai Chem provides specialised logistics services for chemical and pharmaceutical products.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Over the years, it has become a market leader, even supporting MNCs in their overseas operations.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SPRING Singapore's programmes have helped the company develop these specialised capabilities, enhance its information technology (IT) and human resource (HR) systems, and upgrade its workers' skills.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As a result, the company has grown by nearly 13% pa between 2012 and 2016 and created more than 60 good jobs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For other sectors, the focus is on improving productivity and becoming less manpower-intensive.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One example is the accommodation sector, which has achieved notable success over the last two years.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Recently, the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) reported record international visitor arrivals and tourism receipts for a second straight year in 2017.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our hotels, which are a significant part of the accommodation sector, can continue to benefit from Asia’s growing outbound travel only if they can boost productivity and lessen their manpower reliance, while maintaining service quality.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Grand Park City Hall is an example of how this can be done.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I recently visited the hotel which has tapped on STB’s support to adopt manpower-saving technologies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is also part of a new regulatory sandbox with the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and STB that will pilot the use of facial recognition technologies for a seamless check-in process.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Staff can thus be cross deployed to better meet guests' needs in other areas and also learn new skills in the process.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are also working on opportunities that cut across multiple sectors and ITMs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, the growing demand for infrastructure in ASEAN and developing Asia offers significant opportunities that span several industries, including financial services, professional services, precision engineering and construction.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Last year, we introduced the Internationalisation Finance Scheme for Non-Recourse (IFS Non-Recourse) financing scheme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The aim was to help more SMEs participate in regional infrastructure projects, with risk-sharing between the Government and banks for loans that are secured on the project’s cash flow rather than the SME’s assets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This was based on feedback from the industry and an effort to help our SMEs participate in this larger opportunity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Infrastructure Office, which Mr Low Thia Kiang and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah referred to, is a continuation of this effort.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Identifying and structuring infrastructure projects and finding the right partners to finance and execute them remain a challenge both in ASEAN and developing Asia.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Hence, the Infrastructure Office aims to: (a) build a deeper understanding of the pipeline of infrastructure projects in the region; (b) promote collaboration between foreign and local enterprises from the entire infrastructure value chain; and (c) facilitate the structuring, financing and execution of Asian infrastructure projects.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Infrastructure Office will work closely with private sector players – which is the point that Er Dr Lee Bee Wah raised – in the infrastructure ecosystem, supported by Government agencies like ESG, EDB, MAS and the Professional Services Programme Office.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In short, the aim is really to bring together the different players in the infrastructure ecosystem that we have in Singapore – from the public sector, private sector, from the large companies to the small companies, those who do professional services, those who do financial services and those who can execute projects, so that we can bring our capabilities together to address this opportunity as a group.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also had some comments on Government contracts, and I hope she has filed cuts in the MND COS because MND will be better placed to answer that point on construction contracts.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As a whole, our ITMs are inclusive in their design.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Not quite bespoke in the way that Mr Henry Kwek talked about it, but the ITMs aim to address the diverse needs of industries and enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But there is a limit to how many of the over 200,000 enterprises that Government agencies can directly engage.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is why we have stressed the importance of partnerships with TACs, unions and other stakeholders, because they can play an important role to propagate the transformation message and broaden the reach of the ITMs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: While competition is the natural instinct of companies, enterprises can also support one another to succeed in transformation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Currently, EDB and SPRING Singapore support collaborations between large organisations and local SMEs through the PACT programmes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The aim is to allow for knowledge transfer from the bigger companies to the SMEs to support them, for capability development targeted at the SMEs and the test-bedding of innovative solutions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But the important point that Mr Low Thia Khiang makes is that it is also about how it has made a difference for SMEs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is hard to quantify this because some of the impact is qualitative, in terms of capability, but let me use an example.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is the partnership between Onn Wah Precision Engineering, a local precision machining supplier, and Schlumberger’s Singapore Well Testing Centre.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That partnership was to develop high precision machining for oil and gas production instrumentation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This has created a new business opportunity for the company that now accounts for a substantial portion of Onn Wah's total revenue.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: If you take the retail space, the Dairy Farm Group worked with more than 320 SME suppliers to streamline their inventory and supply chain management.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The SME suppliers were better able to track product movements and respond to changes in demand and enjoyed productivity improvements of up to six times in terms of the number of deliveries.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, in short, the overarching emphasis is to deliver benefits to our SMEs in terms of productivity improvement, new capabilities that might, in turn, lead to greater opportunities, the deeper links with their principals and, ultimately, leverage on all of these to go international.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, what sort of programmes will they support?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, in addition to what I have described between the big companies and the SMEs, it is projects amongst SMEs and startups, which will now also qualify for support under the integrated PACT Programme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, the scope of PACT will be expanded to include sourcing for services providers, as well as to promote the early adoption of new technologies among local enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And third, based on feedback from many SMEs on the value of collective branding, resource pooling and venturing overseas together, PACT will also support such strategic alliances to move into new business areas in both domestic and overseas markets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, in other words, it aims to help SMEs complement one another as a group as they venture into new areas, whether it is in Singapore or internationally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Thomas Chua acknowledged that the PACT programme has, indeed, benefited SMEs and that there is a good track record in terms of the outcomes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Like our clusters or sectors, our enterprise landscape is also quite variegated.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Yet, if you look at their share of value add, that has quite the inverse pattern, which is not surprising but it tells us that, on the one hand, we are playing a large numbers game, but with a relatively modest value-add impact and, on the other end of the spectrum, the numbers are few but the value-add impact is significant.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck asked how ESG will support companies at different growth stages.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, ESG will create a more conducive environment for startups by combining SPRING Singapore's Startup SG initiatives and IE Singapore’s international networks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Beyond mentorship and funding, startups increasingly need to internationalise a lot earlier in their development in order to gain access to new markets and also acquire complementary capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Evercomm is a startup that provides end-to-end energy management solutions to help its clients optimise their energy consumption.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: SPRING Singapore provided the company with the Startup SG competitive grant to commercialise its technology, and it also facilitated R&D collaborations with MNCs and foreign players.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Evercomm also tapped on IE Singapore’s networks to navigate overseas markets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Today, the company operates in both Singapore and Taiwan.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Looking ahead, ESG will help Evercomm explore new technology collaborations with partners in Israel, Germany and the US, whilst helping the company expand into the Asia Pacific region.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon will be able to elaborate further on the broader developments that we have in the startup space in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As pointed out by Mr Saktiandi Supaat, many SMEs still require assistance for essential upgrading before they venture overseas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: ESG will work through TACs and industry partners to support them.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This includes the SME Centres, which Mr Thomas Chua referred to, which will continue to be a very important channel for ESG’s SME engagement.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: ESG will also use the new Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) to support the adoption of pre-scoped solutions so that the broad base of SMEs can use them to improve their operational efficiency and productivity.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will be elaborating on these points.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Access to financing is also critical for long-term growth.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: ESG will continue SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore’s partnership with our financial institutions to meet the working capital and growth financing needs of viable SMEs, and to facilitate access to credit lines and insurance cover for trade and projects in overseas markets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The VDP enables local high-growth enterprises to finance their expansion plans with less equity dilution.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Seventeen companies from quite diverse sectors have benefited from the programme since its launch in October 2015.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Thirdly, ESG will support companies to seize overseas opportunities to grow through several internationalisation initiatives.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The importance of internationalisation is borne out by a survey of Singapore's investments abroad by the Department of Statistics from 2006 to 2016, which shows that income from our companies’ direct investment abroad grew by 6.1% pa, higher than the 5.1% pa growth in profits from their operations in Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Looking ahead, one must expect that this differential growth will continue, given the nature and pace of opportunities in the region around us.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: ESG will also enhance IE Singapore’s network of Overseas Centres to help Singapore companies navigate the business and regulatory environment in overseas markets, gain market insights and access to networks with local partners.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As Mr Saktiandi Supaat has observed, to be successful, our SMEs must have the people to navigate different languages and cultures, as well as social, political and legal systems which are quite divergent.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The ASEAN Leadership Programme will help equip Singapore business leaders with a deeper understanding of Southeast Asian markets, and the skillsets to lead business expansions in the region.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will elaborate on this and other related programmes to develop manpower capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ultimately, for our companies to scale up to the next level of growth, capability development, innovation and internationalisation are deeply intertwined.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We see this with companies like Jing King Technology Pte Ltd (JK Tech), that has established itself in chip cards and subscriber identity module (SIM) cards globally.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To expand their business, the company has been exploring R&D in biometrics, electronic payments and data security.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They have built a dedicated R&D team in Singapore, while seeking new opportunities in Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Throughout this journey, they have tapped on Government support, including SPRING Singapore’s CDG as well as IE Singapore’s GCP scheme.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Teo Ser Luck have asked how this will benefit companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think Mr Teo Ser Luck already knows the answers because he was navigating this terrain when he was in MTI.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Nevertheless, EDG will give companies the flexibility to bundle internal upgrading activities, domestic projects and international expansion plans in one application.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, you are able to, in a more flexible and integrated way, plan and seek out Government help for your business strategy.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Even as we pursue these internationalisation and growth strategies, I agree with Mr Leon Perera that succession planning is an important issue for SMEs, especially the family-owned businesses.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In this regard, as Mr Perera has already highlighted, there are several resources that SMEs can tap on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This includes information on succession planning and key issues to look out for on SPRING Singapore's SME Portal.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They can also use the new EDG to engage consultants to help develop the succession plans and address strategic priorities and leadership gaps.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They can also strengthen their leadership pipeline through leadership and management courses which are available under SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But I do want to stress because I think Mr Leon Perera made the point about whether succession planning can be a condition for some of the Government schemes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that may tilt the balance because whilst we can encourage it, we can urge companies to think about this seriously, ultimately, the business owners have to take ownership.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: They have to decide and prioritise that succession planning is something that is of high priority and then undertake specific steps to put that in place.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we have the tool kit, we have the general messaging and the entire gamut of stakeholders, whether it is our trade associations, consultants or Government department officers, they will impart the message.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we have to leave it to the business owners to ultimately make the choices and execute and act on it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: R&D is integral to Singapore’s development and competitiveness.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As Ms Chia Yong Yong has emphasised, this is a long-term endeavour that requires not just thoughtful planning but also perseverance through cycles, because the outcomes may not always be apparent.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We focus on four domains: (a) advanced manufacturing and engineering; (b) health and biomedical sciences; (c) urban solutions and sustainability and (d) services and digital economy.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In all of these domains, there is both a national or broader social benefit possibility as well as an economic benefit possibility.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I do not think the two work at cross purposes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The point that Ms Chia Yong Yong raised was beyond RSEs, what sort of jobs are being created.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: When I describe some of the ecosystem outcomes that we have achieved, it might give you a sense of it although it is difficult to have a direct correlation measurement of the exact outcomes beyond the direct job creation an R&D project may result in.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore's research efforts and outcomes are also acknowledged internationally and by global innovation reports.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It takes into account outcome indicators, such as patent activity, high-tech density, productivity and manufacturing value-add.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are also nurturing public-private R&D partnerships to yield both social and economic benefits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Skin Research Institute of Singapore (SRIS) is a collaboration between A*STAR, the National Skin Centre and Nanyang Technological University (NTU) to build R&D capabilities that can address common medical conditions like eczema, diabetic skin ulcers and tumours.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Such R&D capabilities can also yield economic benefits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, the Ikeda Group, a local SME, has developed novel skincare products using A*STAR’s patented polymeric carrier technology.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The technology allows active ingredients in the skincare serum to be loaded in individual carriers for greater effectiveness.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ikeda launched its new range of serums under the Irén brand in Singapore in December last year and plans to also export it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: More broadly, R&D boosts the innovation capacity and competitiveness of sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Singapore's excellence in skin research has been instrumental in anchoring global industry leaders like P&G, L’Oreal and Amore Pacific.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These MNCs have established skin and hair research labs in Biopolis, which has contributed to the growth of innovation partners, such as ingredients suppliers and contract research organisations (CROs), including university spinoffs, driving the robust and organic expansion of the Consumer Care sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: More broadly, A*STAR offers different avenues of support for enterprises with differing needs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong cited several overseas examples of the modalities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think this slide helps to illustrate the way we are going about it.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This includes, firstly, direct engagement with companies through operations and technology road-mapping or project-specific collaboration agreements.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Second, it can include platforms, like Tech Depot, that offer plug-and-play solutions which address substantially the needs of SMEs which may not have the capacity to undertake bespoke R&D but they are able to adopt broader R&D and technology outcomes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Third, the secondment of researchers to companies under T-Up to conduct R&D and also to develop new products and processes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This is a very successful programme by A*STAR where our researchers are actually seconded out to companies to work in these companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In a not insignificant number of cases, the companies end up hiring them, taking them on full-time.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is a flow of talent that we are quite happy to encourage and support.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And finally, licensing arrangements under the Headstart programme where collaborating companies can tap on royalty-free, exclusive IP from A*STAR for the first 36 months.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are always happy to learn and adapt practices from other jurisdictions in terms of best practices.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Indeed, A*STAR and NRF continue to do this on an active basis.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To punch above our weight and position Singapore as the Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, we must have our finger on the pulse of global trends and ensure that our institutions are ready to respond to emerging opportunities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: That is why A*STAR is proactively transforming itself to stay at the forefront of science and technology trends, help enterprises capture opportunities and attain higher levels of R&D outcomes and aspirations over the long term.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Over the past two decades, A*STAR has nurtured a strong base of capabilities to support the innovation capacity of our industries.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In general, I think we are going in the right direction.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But more can be done and today's research and innovation landscape in Singapore and around the world is vastly different from that a decade ago.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We must expect that it will continue to evolve.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, we are encouraging our firms to be more innovative and transform.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Equally, we want our public sector agencies to also become nimbler and be better partners to enterprises on their innovation and transformation journey.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A*STAR aims to be more agile and flexible in the way it is able to harness research talent and funds to develop capabilities and skills at the leading edge and then transfer these technologies to industries in an even more efficacious manner than in the past.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A*STAR will do so primarily through a mechanism they call programmes that will bring together multidisciplinary teams from various institutions in Singapore in order to solve complex problems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Increasingly, many of the problems are of a multidisciplinary nature.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You need not just someone from an engineering domain.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: You may need mathematicians, biologists and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This sort of structure is flexible and is able to draw on the talent that is needed in order to start addressing the more complex problems.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: An example of this is A*STAR's AI Initiative.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It was launched recently in collaboration with the universities and industry.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One of the solutions developed by the cross-disciplinary team under A*STAR AI is an automated real-time fault detection tool for predictive maintenance.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This system has already been adopted by a few companies in the engineering and transportation sectors.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: A*STAR will elaborate further on its transformation process in due course.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Our universities are also undertaking more industry relevant research, the importance of which Ms Foo Mee Har emphasised.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Beyond the examples I have shared of the linkages between A*STAR and industry, the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) framework for the allocation of research funding to autonomous universities also takes into account industry collaboration, such as the number of industry projects and the amount of industry co-funding for R&D.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is on the uptick and we are seeing more of this happening.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Funding models that are being used by NRF and the broader Research, Innovation and Enterprise Council (RIEC) system encourage more of these interagency collaborations together with the private sector.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: International collaborations also help us to stay abreast of global research and industry developments.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Campus for Research Excellence and Technological Enterprise (CREATE) brings together local and international researchers from diverse backgrounds to work on areas of strategic interest.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This helps with knowledge transfer, capability-building and cross-fertilisation of ideas.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: One other initiative that is taking us closer to the vision of becoming a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise is GIA, something that the Finance Minister talked about, and many Members would already have heard about.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The aim is to create linkages with global startup hubs, to help entrepreneurs and students gain access to the global innovation network and work with like-minded companies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Members would notice that several or the majority of these are Asian cities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is actually a deliberate effort on our part to develop a deeper innovation network in Asia and also within ASEAN.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The aim at the end of the day is to serve as an in-market entry point for Singapore entities to connect with the business and innovation community in these cities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Over the next four years, GIA will expand its reach across ASEAN and to other startup hubs around the world.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Around the world, we know that countries are taking active steps to reduce their reliance on fossil fuels and meet their climate change targets.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Against this backdrop, it is also in the interest of our companies to become more energy-efficient and reduce their carbon footprint.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: This will help all businesses adjust to the new system and encourage them to reduce emissions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We will closely monitor our economic competitiveness, international climate change developments, and the progress in meeting our emissions abatement goals, and factor these into any future reviews of the carbon tax.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Meanwhile, we will also set aside funds from 2019 to enhance support for companies, including SMEs and power generation companies, to improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Besides promoting energy efficiency on the demand side, we are also adapting policies on the supply side to better serve the needs of businesses and households.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: For example, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) has progressively liberalised the retail electricity market to allow more consumers the flexibility of choosing an electricity retailer and price plan that best meet their needs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have steadily lowered the threshold for contestability to the present average monthly electricity consumption of at least 2,000 kWh.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: To date, about 50%, or about 49,000 accounts, of businesses that are eligible for contestability have switched to buying electricity from a retailer of their choice.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Charles Chong has asked what consumers can expect from market liberalisation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The OEM will allow the remaining small businesses and households the same flexibility that I have just described.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: These consumers will receive a notification letter and information booklet from EMA in the next few weeks, which will explain how they can benefit from greater choice and flexibility in their electricity purchases.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Retailers are also expected to start marketing to Jurong consumers towards the end of March.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Charles Chong is correct in expressing some concerns about whether consumers will be inundated with marketing materials.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: EMA has been working closely with the retailers to have a Code of Conduct, if you will, in terms of how they can market their products and to minimise the kind of confusion or stress that may be caused at the consumer end.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: There will be an online platform which can help consumers to easily compare the standard price plans offered by different retailers.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And those who prefer to stay with Singapore Power (SP) on the regulated tariff can continue to do so and they will be no worse-off.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, Chairman, if I can summarise, the new economic opportunities and challenges that I have outlined also call for new approaches.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Everyone needs to transform, but no two transformation journeys are the same.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Each company and sector must find its own path, based on its unique circumstances.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The Government will provide resources and support for companies to develop their capabilities, to innovate and to internationalise, no matter what their starting point is.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The need to transform applies not just to individuals, enterprises and industries, but equally to Government agencies.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We have not shied away from reinventing ourselves, both in terms of organisational structures and processes, for example, in the formation of ESG and some of the work that A*STAR is undertaking, and also in relation to our policies and programmes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are changing, consolidating or adapting our programmes to new requirements in the market.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We believe, ultimately, it will take the collective effort of all stakeholders for this transformation to succeed.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We also believe that if all of us come together, with all hands on deck, we can position ourselves well to achieve sustainable growth and opportunities for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, over the past year, I have had the opportunity to meet and listen to many SME business leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They see the world changing around them and know the urgency of transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, consumer markets in the region are growing, and there is much goodwill towards Singaporean brands and products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, technology has enabled new business models to flourish and sharpen businesses' competitive edges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I believe SMEs want to know what concrete steps they can take to seize these opportunities and remain relevant and competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government knows that it can be daunting to try new business strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why we, and our many partners, have committed to working with our SMEs throughout their transformation journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The formation of ESG is a natural progression, born of the recognition that capability-building, innovation and internationalisation are increasingly intertwined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister for Industry Iswaran has already spoken on how ESG will combine the expertise, resources and networks of SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore to build on their good work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck raised the question many SMEs have on their minds: how exactly will ESG and EDG affect the Government's support for their businesses?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: EDG is one grant, with a single application process, combining SPRING Singapore's CDG and IE Singapore's GCP scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will give more holistic assistance to companies who can make use of the same grant to upgrade, innovate or venture overseas, or any combination of these strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This, in turn, encourages companies to think holistically about their own growth strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Castlery has worked together with both SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore for capability building and internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At home, Castlery built up its internal capabilities by developing a warehouse management system with the help of SPRING Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This system optimised Castlery’s warehouse space and inventory management, resulting in a significant increase in inventory capacity and sales per worker.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This allowed Castlery to scale its operations quickly as it expanded overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In venturing abroad, Castlery tapped on IE Singapore's support and network of business contacts to quickly penetrate the market in Australia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The two agencies’ support and grants have helped Castlery achieve faster growing sales and the launch of its flagship store in Sydney in July last year, its first overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And there are many other companies that have benefited in a similar manner from SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore’s support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the establishment of ESG in April 2018, enterprises like Castlery will have a single key point of contact at ESG rather than working with SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore separately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Enterprises will be able to discuss their growth strategies with ESG to determine the best grants and programmes for their stage of growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: EDG can support solutions of a very complex nature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For businesses that want simpler solutions for improving productivity, pre-scoped productivity solutions are a tried and tested way to achieve quick results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past few years, our businesses have benefited from various grants supporting basic productivity upgrading, such as SPRING Singapore’s ICV.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Now, as businesses enter the next phase of transformation, they may require more substantial investments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PSG, announced by the Minster for Finance, will offer pre-scoped solutions developed in conjunction with industries’ lead agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how it will improve support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PSG will support the adoption of IT solutions and equipment aligned to the ITM strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One example of an industry-specific solution that will be supported under PSG is the Digital Ordering and Payment System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: ENBU, a Japanese restaurant in Suntec City, adopted a version of this system with support from SPRING Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The solution combines both Tabsquare’s e-menu solution with PayPal's payment solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Customers have the freedom to order and pay without delay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is no need to wait for staff to serve them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If customers have concerns about entering their payment details on an unfamiliar device, they can also complete the payment on their own phones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For ENBU, the system has reduced cash handling, and increased productivity and efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The solution has also freed ENBU’s staff to better serve customers’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope to see more companies adopt similar solutions to enhance their productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To enable them to do so, we will continue to simplify the overall grant landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: PSG will be one of the grants on the Business Grants Portal (BGP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Teo Ser Luck asked how we can continue making it simpler for business to learn about assistance schemes and transact with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: BGP represents one way that the Government has been responding to these calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Rather than approaching multiple agencies on their grants, a company only needs to fill in its project information on BGP's shorter, simpler online forms, and the relevant agency will process the application.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Because the BGP stores and pre-populates basic information like a company’s details, forms can be filled more quickly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a result, BGP has been very well-received by companies since its launch in January 2017, and nine out of 10 indicated that they were satisfied with the portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another way the Government has been making Government transactions more business-friendly is LicenceOne.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Launched in 2016, LicenceOne is an online portal that helps businesses comply with regulations through simplified licence application processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: LicenceOne's e-Advisor feature will shortlist relevant licences based on applicants' business needs and intent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am encouraged by the feedback from businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Nine out of 10 surveyed indicated that the portal is easy to use, and that they would recommend LicenceOne as the go-to place for licensing-related matters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hope that these initiatives will simplify transaction processes for businesses with the Government, an especially pertinent point in the business environment, where time is money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More grants and licences will be added to BGP and LicenceOne respectively over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government will continue to look out for ways to make these processes more business-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When it comes to supporting our enterprises, the Government does not act alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our TACs are also key partners of our business community in industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: TACs have deep knowledge of their industry and are well-placed to address key issues facing the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They help their members adapt to changes in the business environment, stay ahead of the curve, and make inroads into overseas markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also act as a bridge between the Government and businesses, enhancing collaborations and expanding reach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have seen TACs within and across industries step up and work together to support our enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Minister for Finance has mentioned the Logistics Alliance and SCCCI's Trade Association Hub (TA Hub).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These initiatives facilitate the cross-pollination of ideas and help advance common interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In particular, the physical infrastructure of the TA Hub creates chances for TACs to interact informally, building a stronger TAC community based on mutual support and collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That six more TACs have decided to join the 25 already in the TA Hub since its launch in November 2017 is testament that our TACs believe in the value of co-location, cooperation and collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Thomas Chua have observed, our TACs are excellent multipliers and catalysts for industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government will continue to support our TACs to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The LEAD Programme is SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore’s flagship grant for TACs to drive industry initiatives, focusing on areas, such as internationalisation, technology and infrastructure, and business collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: LEAD was launched in 2005, and we have continually reviewed the scheme to improve our support to TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are other programmes administered by various agencies that have similar objectives and funding support to TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Grants to TACs, such as SPRING Singapore's LEAD+ and TAC-led Collaborative Industry Projects, as well as STB’s Association Development Fund, will come under the consolidated LEAD.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, LEAD will support place management initiatives, by funding TAC-led projects under the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) pilot Business Improvement District (BID) scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With consolidated LEAD support, TACs can spearhead holistic upgrading strategies that combine capability development with place management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: ESG will work closely with URA and STB to ensure TACs can more easily understand and access the support to enable them in their industry transformation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government and TACs have strengthened the support system in place for SMEs to transform and grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The time is ripe for SMEs to step up in the journey of transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are SMEs which have taken the initiative to transform themselves, to laudable results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa has noted, it has been a year since the launch of the Lifestyle cluster ITMs and there has been good traction for their strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Henry Kwek has asked for examples on specific initiatives to help industries in transformation and restructuring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To grow the top line, the Government and its key partners implement ITM strategies to help companies innovate and access new market segments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our SMEs have, from time to time, asked how they can access the benefits of our investments in technology and scientific research.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Iswaran mentioned that the Centres of Innovation are key multipliers for our ITMs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Centres of Innovation set up by SPRING Singapore in partnership with selected polytechnics and research institutes, harness their laboratory facilities, skilled manpower and considerable networks to develop innovative technological solutions for SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NuHoney is a local company that first started working with FIRC on product development in 2011.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: After four years of R&D, it successfully launched its product, a carbonated honey beverage made with no added sugar.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The product won the Singapore Institute of Food Science and Technology’s Food Product Award for Innovation in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NuHoney is already back to working with FIRC to develop new variants, with the export potential in mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: ITM strategies are also tailored to address industry pain points.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For the Lifestyle cluster, manpower initiatives are developed in close consultation with the industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We hear feedback from the food services, retail and hotel industries that the human touch is indispensable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To them, good service is a point of pride.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why the Skills Frameworks for each of these feature delivery of good service and improvement of customer experience as key skills in customer-serving roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some Lifestyle cluster companies may equate being productive and manpower-lean with poorer service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: By applying good design, it is possible to make processes more efficient while making customers happier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, Shangri-La Hotel embarked on an optimisation exercise supported by STB.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It found that there were several inefficiencies in the operations of its Horizon Club lounge on the Executive Floor.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Staff had to walk to opposite ends of the building or go up and down floors to get to the kitchen and storage rooms, leading to unnecessary delays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the retrofit, Shangri-La sited the kitchen and storage areas next to the lounge and introduced self-service options that were designed to enhance guests' experiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the self-service bar, featuring a wide range of wines and spirits, guests can try their hand at mixing their own cocktails according to the provided recipes, or even invent one of their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the self-service options, and faster service from staff who can be more attentive to guests' needs, the retrofitted Horizon Club has been very well-received.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Productive technologies also mean that staff spend less time on routine or tedious tasks, and more time providing better service to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, Tourego is a homegrown company that developed the world's first mobile tourist tax refund solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the Tourego app, visitors can have their tax refund tickets issued and stored in-app and no longer need to keep paper tickets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
