text: For retailers, staff do not have to manually take down tourists' personal details, saving time and manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To make Tourego possible, STB worked with Tourego and the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) to ensure it obtained the necessary licences, and MTI's Pro-Enterprise Panel facilitated cooperation with Government agencies to ensure Tourego's solution complemented existing systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Innovation and design will continue to be vital tools for companies and remain a cornerstone in the development of brands in the Lifestyle industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is our hope that more of our brands will become household names and fly our flag overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is no lack of energy, ideas or passion among existing or aspiring Singapore brand owners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In food, we have established names like BreadTalk, Old Chang Kee, Jumbo Group and Peach Garden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Companies are diversifying and creating new products and offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Foodgnostic, through its retail brand Old Seng Choong, sells traditional festive treats with a twist.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In fashion, which faces intense competition from both global and local brands, we do not just have Charles & Keith.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Produced by the DesignSingapore Council in collaboration with Singaporean tastemaker Daniel Boey, the book showcases the diversity and depth of Singapore design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There are brands like In Good Company with its women's wear and accessories, Carrie K's premium artisan-crafted jewellery, and Ling Wu’s exotic skin bags and accessories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Singapore Fashion Black Book was also created in partnership with Commune, a homegrown furniture design and lifestyle company that sells sophisticated pieces for the modern home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We must continue creating opportunities for our local companies and talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are building the platforms to support Singapore’s growing ecosystem of lifestyle brands and our wellspring of design talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a retail showcase featuring local brands, it will increase the presence of local designers along Orchard Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As an incubation space, it will provide holistic support to local designers in capability development and internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Sixty local brands will be housed at the retail showcase, which will host monthly events for Design Orchard's visitors to get to know our local brands and designers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Design Orchard will complement the ground-up efforts of our community, such as Carolyn Kan’s KEEPERS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Currently housed in the National Design Centre, KEEPERS curates homegrown lifestyle brands and tells the story of Singapore talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Economic transformation is a long-haul journey which requires the participation of all our enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While it is important to ensure the successful transformation of large enterprises, we must not overlook the other smaller enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such SMEs may be of smaller scale, but they have a significant presence due to their large numbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: After all, many of these SMEs and micro-enterprises provide essential services for our citizens' daily life, such as those in the food and retail industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The most direct way to enable our citizens on the ground to feel the impact of economic transformation is to support these SMEs and micro-enterprises to transform and upgrade, so that they can provide new and better consumer experiences for the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These heartland enterprises can be said to be unique to Singapore and are deeply linked to our HDB culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The rise of the digital economy continues to disrupt many businesses’ operating environments, including those of the micro-enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Though many heartland shops still maintain a loyal base of customers who prefer the traditional way that heartland enterprises operate, younger customers have a different set of expectations in terms of the goods and services, and even the mode of communication and payment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are also experts at online shopping and enjoy the convenience of items delivered right to their doorsteps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: How our heartland enterprises can, with their small footprints, transform to attract younger customers while serving their more traditional customers will be key to their continued success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chen Show Mao brought up the importance of diversity and vibrancy in our heartlands and suggested rental rebates as a potential approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government closely monitors the property markets to ensure the stability and sustainability of rentals for businesses over the medium to long term.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To ensure that our HDB Neighbourhood Centres and precincts remain vibrant places for residents and businesses alike, HDB has adopted the following measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: When planning commercial spaces, HDB would take into consideration the number of residents and future development plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, when assessing bids for HDB shops, HDB would not only consider the rent which the bidder is willing to pay, but also the quality of the bidder's business concept.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many of the micro-enterprises have banded together to form various trade associations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One example is working with various Government agencies to develop pilot precinct development plans for Bedok and Ang Mo Kio to revitalise the area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This example shows the Government's commitment in supporting TACs which have the resolve to transform, and working hand-in-hand with them to help enterprises to improve productivity, innovate, internationalise and upgrade skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: After all, there are over 200,000 enterprises in Singapore and the majority is made up of SMEs and micro-enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is not sufficient to solely depend on the Government’s one-on-one efforts to send the message of transformation to every single enterprise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: TACs can amplify the reach of the Government's transformation efforts, and working closely with the TACs is a key component to successful industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government welcomes more TACs to work with us and get more enterprises to join us on this transformation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Transformation does not have to be daunting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has transformed itself and made it easier for our SMEs to take charge of their own upgrading and internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Together with our partners, we have created an environment for SMEs to seize the opportunities that the future economy presents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To my fellow Members, if you are approached for help about how enterprises can benefit from the Government schemes, I want to reassure you that, at every step of an SME's journey, there is support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For SMEs seeking easy-to-digest solutions, they can check the SME Portal, access the BGP, or approach any of the 12 SME Centres island-wide for free business advice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For SMEs looking for more complex support, they can look to grants like the EDG or start a discussion with ESG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Throughout this, TACs will continue to spearhead initiatives that enhance the competitiveness and relevance of their industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For those enterprises that have benefited from the Government’s and TACs' support, I urge you to share your experience with your business community and help spread the culture of mutual help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For enterprises that are not already a member of a TAC, I encourage you to join one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Technological advancements have had a profound impact on our industries and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Although change can be disruptive, it presents many opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, may I have your permission to display some slides on the LED screens later on in my speech, please.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Manufacturing remains an important pillar of Singapore’s economy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, we have a diversified portfolio of high value-added manufacturing industries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Our products are exported to many markets globally.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In 2017, Singapore’s manufacturing sector saw strong growth, and the sector continued to expand at a robust pace in January 2018.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are witnessing rapid technological developments in areas, such as robotics and the industrial Internet-of-Things (IoT).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One, it is to establish Singapore as a globally-competitive advanced manufacturing hub.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will help attract strategic investments and anchor our position in global value chains.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Two, it is for our companies to gain a competitive advantage by prioritising three areas: (a) undertaking innovation; (b) adopting technologies, and (c) preparing their workers to thrive in tomorrow’s workforce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In Mandarin):   In my English speech, I said that we must prioritise three things to achieve a competitive advantage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One, undertaking innovation; two, adopting technologies; and three, preparing workers to thrive in tomorrow's workplace.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Innovation is key to differentiating oneself from the competition.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This can take the form of creating new products, finding business opportunities, and developing efficient means to optimise resources.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some manufacturing subsectors, such as precision engineering (PE), are already seeing the need for innovation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One of the ways that SMEs can improve their innovation capacity is by tapping on A*STAR's Growing Enterprises through Technology Upgrade (GET-Up) initiative, which offers Operation and Technology Roadmapping (OTR).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Through OTR, SMEs can get A*STAR's guidance to customise a long-term growth strategy to realise new product or service offerings.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The OTR provides SMEs with business strategies to assess consumer demand, challenges and potential markets.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It originally focused on manufacturing connectors and capacitors for the electronics industry.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Through OTR, it has discovered opportunities in the automotive market.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It invested around $1.7 million in equipment and infrastructure, hired a team of engineers to develop automotive components and entered new markets in 2016.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We hope that more companies will see the value of innovation and enjoy similar benefits.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To extend the reach of OTR, A*STAR will work through lead Government agencies and TACs to launch consortium-style OTRs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will bring together companies within the same sub-sector to chart out technology roadmaps for shared problem statements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Participating companies can then build on these shared roadmaps as base templates to further customise solutions for their needs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This arrangement allows more companies to leverage shared resources, such as industry experts and technology developers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The first consortium-style OTR will bring together 16 food manufacturing companies, including Kee Song Group and Phoon Huat Pte Ltd, to identify common technology areas to improve productivity.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These include shopfloor control systems and shelf-life monitoring solutions to reduce food waste.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Besides improving innovation capacity, SMEs can adopt manufacturing technologies to optimise their processes and resources.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This ensures that companies remain competitive and can benefit from upturns in external demand, as demonstrated by the strong productivity growth in the electronics and precision engineering clusters in 2017.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In those clusters, real value-added per worker grew by 35% and 15% respectively.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To facilitate the adoption of technologies, we have put in place various support schemes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For companies considering the deployment of large-scale automation to improve productivity, SPRING Singapore offers the Automation Support Package (ASP) comprising grant, tax and loan incentives to offset costs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One local company which has tapped on the ASP is Lingjack, a manufacturer of firefighting equipment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Lingjack previously depended on manual labour for almost 90% of its manufacturing processes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Through ASP, the company introduced new equipment to automate functions, such as polishing, welding and leak testing.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a result, Lingjack improved its manufacturing efficiency by almost 40% and is looking to expand its production capacity.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is also looking to manufacture higher value-added goods and is targeting an increase in revenue by up to 20% this year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Companies which are looking for ready technology solutions can access the Tech Depot, jointly created by A*STAR, IMDA and SPRING Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is an online repository of plug-and-play productivity solutions which can be found on SPRING Singapore's SME Portal.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The solutions cover areas, such as inventory and asset tracking and supply chain management.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Even as companies review their strategies and plans, they should transform with their workers in mind.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We strongly encourage companies to proactively prepare their workers for the changes ahead.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Univac, a precision engineering large local enterprise (LLE) that manufactures medical devices and life science consumables, is one such company.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Univac not only embarked on transforming its business, but is also equipping its employees for the changes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yim Kong Ming, 59, is a Senior Quality Engineer with the company.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: His job used to be very manual, requiring significant time and effort for data collection.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Today, as Univac incorporates software applications in its processes, data collection is increasingly automated and seamless.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These ongoing changes allow its workers to be redeployed to higher value-added tasks, such as data analysis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To prepare its employees for the changes, Univac assembled a team to provide training in the new software and technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The team also provides on-the-job support during the implementation phase to ensure that the engineers and technicians are competent and confident in operating the software.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Kong Ming appreciates how the digital transformation has made his job less laborious.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Instead of having to manually collect the data, he has easy access to it on his digital devices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: He can focus more on data analysis and problem resolution.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: (In English): Over time, as our companies continue to improve their innovation capacity, adopt technologies and prepare their workforce, we will build up a strong local manufacturing base to support our vision of being an advanced manufacturing hub.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: While I have spoken about the many schemes available to support companies, I understand that some companies are unsure how and where to begin their transformation journey.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And this is a point Mr Sitoh Yih Pin raised earlier.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a first step, companies can use EDB's Singapore Smart Industry Readiness Index (SSIRI).

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This tool will help companies to self-diagnose the future-readiness of their organisational processes, technology usage and workforce skills.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is designed to be used by companies of all sizes in all sectors to determine how they may implement "smart" manufacturing operations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I encourage companies to sign up for the SSIRI workshops conducted by EDB to find out more.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I will also speak more about the SSIRI later this month at the IoT Asia Conference 2018.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I would now like to speak about the Government’s efforts to maintain Singapore’s competitiveness as a global trade hub.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, the wholesale trade sector is lesser known to many Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The sector is also external-facing, with over 80% of sales derived from international trade.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This international aspect puts the wholesale trade sector in a prime position for growth over the next decade.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Across Asia, rapid population growth and rising consumerism are expected to fuel regional demand for goods like food, fuel and smart devices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To help local enterprises unlock these opportunities, the Government has worked to deepen our trade connections with ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In September 2017, the Singapore Logistics Association (SLA) and Global eTrade Services (GeTS) launched "hive", a regional B2B trade facilitation platform. "Hive" supports companies in meeting cross-border trade compliance requirements for over 50 customs authorities in ASEAN and around the world.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This allows companies to enjoy greater process efficiencies and seamless clearance, since "hive" will be linked to Singapore Customs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Yet, we must be prepared for how technological advancements, such as blockchain technology and data analytics, could revolutionise the way global trade is conducted in the coming years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This new fund, TIDF, will be offered as a grant to support companies which are looking to develop B2B e-marketplaces and innovative trade solutions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: TIDF will also support initiatives to create a wider spectrum of financial value-added service offerings.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These efforts will help support our wholesale trade companies to scale up and become more productive and innovative.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will speak in greater detail about how our people can thrive in this new environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Much of my speech has focused on transforming and rejuvenating existing industries to future-proof Singapore’s economy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I would now like to address another part of the equation and, that is, how the Government is working to nurture startups as catalysts of growth.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Charles Chong asked about the Government’s efforts to build up our startup landscape.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Startups play an important role in our economy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They help to boost Singapore’s economic competitiveness through innovative ideas and disruption of existing industries, thus contributing to sector development and transformation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In recent years, we have seen good growth in the number, contribution and quality of our startups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In particular, the number of tech startups increased from 2,800 to 4,300 in the same period, employing about 24,000 workers in 2016.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Startups in Singapore are also attracting a good level of investor interest and funding.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In January 2018, local logistics startup Ninja Van raised over US$87 million in its Series C funding round, while late last year, homegrown gaming company Razer raised US$528 million in its initial public offering in Hong Kong.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: These developments reflect the growing quality and potential of startups here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This shows that our moves to distinguish Singapore’s startup scene through establishing a strong brand identity, strengthening our talent attraction efforts, and enhancing funding support are bearing fruit. "Startup SG" was launched in March 2017 as a single brand identity to showcase Singapore’s startup ecosystem to the world.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It also unified the Government's startup support schemes, making it easier for entrepreneurs to apply for support.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore leveraged the Startup SG brand to organise the inaugural Startup SG competition, SLINGSHOT@SWITCH, in September 2017.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The competition attracted more than 900 teams from over 30 countries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Media coverage of the competition and the Startup SG brand was extensive and helped to increase global mindshare of Singapore as a startup hub.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Second, to improve Singapore's attractiveness to global entrepreneurial talent, we enhanced the EntrePass scheme’s entry and renewal criteria in August 2017.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since then, the number of applications has more than doubled.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Given Singapore’s small size, we need to remain open to promising global entrepreneurial talent who can contribute to the vibrancy of our startup scene.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will help to seed future growth and good local jobs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In 2016, foreign startups generated a total of 9,800 local jobs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As a percentage share of the total employment generated by foreign startups, local jobs took up 54%, which constitutes an increase from 50% in 2012.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In one example, after Dr Bert Grobben's application for the EntrePass was supported in 2015, he incorporated a startup here called Budding Innovations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: His company specialises in commercialisation of technology by working with companies to develop go-to-market strategies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Budding Innovations has since created five local jobs, of which three are PMETs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Third, to strengthen funding support, we raised the cap and proportion of the Government’s co-investment funding share under Startup SG Equity last year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This aims to catalyse private sector investment into promising Singapore-based technology startups with IP and global market potential.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Beyond funding, the deep tech startups will stand to benefit from the resources and know-how provided by those various co-investment partners, which had been chosen for their expertise in the respective sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This includes help with technology translation, prototyping and manufacturing facilities, and strategic networks for development and commercialisation, thus working to shorten the startups’ learning curves and improving their chances of success.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To scale up, startups should seek out-growth opportunities, both locally and abroad.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Startups can tap on partner networks which we have put into place.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Last year, the Government worked closely with partners like the Action Community for Entrepreneurship (ACE) to strengthen startups’ access to smart financing and global networks.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This included supporting the launch of ACE International Centre, which provides a landing pad for global startups and helps local startups to scale up and internationalise.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: JTC has also developed LaunchPads at one-north and Jurong Innovation District (JID), which offer a range of spaces for startups to operate in and testbed their ideas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: More importantly, LaunchPads serve as hubs to connect entrepreneurs with accelerators, incubators, venture capitalists and fellow entrepreneurs in related fields.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This creates opportunities for knowledge sharing, collaboration and growth.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: At JTC LaunchPad@JID, JTC will work with partners to provide a one-stop prototyping centre where deep tech startups can leverage shared equipment for small batch production.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: SPRING Singapore will also be launching the Startup SG (SSG) Network later this year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The SSG Network will be a one-stop database of information, as well as an e-community of startups and ecosystem players.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will support networking and facilitate business matching for startups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: With the establishment of ESG in April this year, startups will be able to leverage ESG’s international network of offices and in-market partners to scale up and expand into new overseas markets.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: ESG will advise startups on capability development and internationalisation, while providing them with integrated support through the schemes that were previously under SPRING Singapore and IE Singapore.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As the Minister for Industry, Mr S Iswaran, had earlier highlighted that the Government is adapting to better serve the needs of industry in Singapore’s new economic environment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Besides the CPFTA, CCS will continue its current mandate of administering the Competition Act.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I would now like to address Mr Lim Biow Chuan's question about consumer protection for online transactions, specifically his suggestions to restrict the use of mandatory arbitration clauses in standard terms and conditions and pre-ticked boxes for additional goods and services.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Act provides for civil actions to be taken by consumers and by specified bodies against retailers that persist in unfair trading practices.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Government adopts a balanced approach of supporting a pro-enterprise environment, while at the same time protecting consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In line with the principle of the freedom of contract, businesses are free to enter into consumer contracts, as long as it is mutually agreed to by the contracting parties.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Businesses and consumers should be alert to the clauses and conditions of any contract they enter into, including the fine print.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Consumers should also take steps to protect themselves before making their purchases.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This could include checking reviews on the reputation of retailers as well as their refund policies and mechanisms.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Practices, such as using small print to conceal or mislead consumers on a material fact in relation to the transaction, can be considered as unfair practices under CPFTA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We note Mr Lim Biow Chuan's suggestions on arbitration clauses and pre-ticked boxes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We will continue to monitor the situation and take appropriate actions, if necessary.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I have elaborated in my speech, the Government has in place extensive support structures and initiatives to support our SMEs and startups on their transformation journey.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What remains is for companies to step up and make the right investments today to seize new growth opportunities not just for themselves, but also for a better future for all of us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, Minister Lim Hng Kiang, Minister Iswaran, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon have spoken about how our economy has to transform.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We face global trends, such as the shift in economic weight towards Asia and the emergence of new technologies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: What does this mean for our people, Singaporeans?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: All of us, whether as students, employees and business owners, need to constantly learn, constantly adapt, and constantly embrace new skills and knowledge all the time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As the Government, we will strive to enable our people for the future, especially through (a) the deepening of relevant skills; and (b) the nurturing of global market expertise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Yee Chia Hsing and Miss Cheryl Chan talked about the importance of continuous skills upgrading in today’s evolving economic landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree that our people need to be enabled with the relevant skills for jobs today and in the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That is why it is absolutely crucial for every Singaporean to make lifelong learning a way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are fostering this cultural change through initiatives, such as the national SkillsFuture movement as well as the Adapt and Grow programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While we recognise that continuing education and training may not be easy due to many competing demands on our time, it is a necessary investment so that we can stay ahead for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The changing economic landscape means that for some people, mid-career switches have become necessary.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The types of jobs available may be different as some sectors undergo restructuring.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For those looking to make a career switch into a different sector, the Government has developed a suite of Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) under the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The PCPs are career conversion programmes which help mid-career jobseekers, including PMETs, to reskill and move into new occupations and sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In partnership with Workforce Singapore (WSG), our economic agencies are working closely with companies as well as TACs to train and place local PMETs in these sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Members have just heard from Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon talk about the Wholesale Trade sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will also use this sector as an example.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the Wholesale Trade sector, IE Singapore, Singapore Management University, International Chamber of Commerce Academy and WSG jointly developed a PCP called International Trading PCP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This provides training for the fundamental skills and knowledge of international trade, such as digital marketing, procurement, supply chain management and logistics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, it has been about seven to eight months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Kenny Ang is amongst those who has benefited from the International Trading PCP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: After having worked in the Food Services sector for about seven years, Mr Ang was keen to make a career switch.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Despite his lack of experience in Wholesale Trade, he was able, through the PCP, to pick up the relevant skills and knowledge that are needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Ang has since found employment with Raduga Pte Ltd, a distributor of mobility solutions and mobile phones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: He manages the company's marketing campaigns and branding projects with regional partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The International Trading PCP is but only one of the many PCPs available.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MOM will be giving further updates on the Adapt and Grow initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, please allow me to continue in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Just a while ago, I talked about the PCP and how it has helped more mature workers to make a mid-career switch by learning new skills to handle new jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we develop more training programmes, it is crucial to ensure that these programmes meet industry needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Therefore, during the process of developing the ITMs, the Government has worked closely with employers, TACs, as well as trade unions, to identify the skills required in the relevant industries, and incorporate these skills into the skills framework of various industries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: When an individual and company develops a training programme, everything becomes clear once they refer to the skills framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have also launched the Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) framework for 31 technical skills and competencies, and nine generic skills and competencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As we push for industry transformation and skills upgrading, employers are our most critical partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One example is Hewlett Packard (HP) Singapore, which has actively groomed local talent through programmes, such as the learning platform "Brain Candy" and other graduate programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These training initiatives in new fields, like 3D printing and data analytics, enable their employees to keep up with changes in the industry and cope with new jobs and new demands.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In response to the SkillsFuture Programme, HP recently introduced 20 employees as Growth Mindset Ambassadors under an inhouse initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These ambassadors will be tasked with promoting lifelong learning throughout the organisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government urges more employers to promote training for their workers and encourage workers to upgrade their skills, just like HP Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With the rapid development of new technologies, every company has to keep pace with the changes in disruptive technologies, and ensure their employees continue to grow, so that their company continues to grow as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It is often said that a hardworking employee is a good employee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Similarly, employers who encourage employees to work hard and learn are also good employers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Companies that take training seriously and reward employees accordingly will also be able to attract and retain good workers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ultimately, if employees are equipped with industry-relevant skills that enhance their productivity and support the growth of the company, employers also stand to benefit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Hence, promoting skills upgrading amongst employees is the ultimate key to maintaining the long-term competitiveness of businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): My colleagues have highlighted the need for companies to venture beyond our shores, especially to the rest of Asia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A lack of familiarity with overseas markets is often cited by companies as the biggest obstacle to internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Mr Yee Chia Hsing that our enterprises and our people need to develop greater global market expertise to capture Asia's potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These programmes are targeted at individuals across a range of ages and levels of experience, from our young students to our current and future business leaders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For our students, we have the SkillsFuture Young Talent Programme (YTP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: YTP provides our students with opportunities for overseas internships and work-study programmes in the fast-growing Asian markets, including Southeast Asia.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is ITE College Central's Ms Lim Siying.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Last December, Siying spent a stint working at Big C Supercenter in Lamphun, Thailand.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: During her stint with the hypermart operator, Siying led a group of 18 trainees and managed the inventory, labelling and a promotional campaign for the cosmetics section.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Siying shared with us that this exposure has sparked her interest in the different Southeast Asian markets.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: She observed that the different Southeast Asian markets have diverse leadership and business styles.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: She shared that the stint has also broadened her horizons and led her to make many friends overseas.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And she is quite sure that whether she works for a company or if she becomes a business owner, these friendships with many different nationalities will serve her very well throughout her lifetime.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And that is the impact we hope to make via YTP.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Thus, YTP not only offers students valuable opportunities for cross-cultural learning, they also learn to venture out of their comfort zones and build networks in today's increasingly interconnected world.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: How about our current and future business leaders?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Our current and future business leaders are able to tap on SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) to enhance their growth and international exposure to key overseas markets.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier, Minister Iswaran also spoke about the LDI ASEAN Leadership Programme.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The ASEAN Leadership Programme offers opportunities for business leaders, current and future, to gain overseas market immersion and training that are vital for the development of their global market expertise.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: As our Singapore companies expand throughout ASEAN and beyond, it is crucial that we have a pipeline of talent ready to lead and support these efforts.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The ASEAN Leadership Programme will focus on creating a vibrant pool of business leaders who understand the unique business environments and cultures of Southeast Asian markets.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These countries offer significant growth opportunities for our companies, especially as ASEAN continues to integrate.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: By 2030, ASEAN could become the fourth largest single market in the world, after China, the US and the EU.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: With more than 600 million people, and a middle class that is expected to increase from 38 million households in 2015 to 161 million middle-class households in 2030, ASEAN has lots of promise and untapped potential.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Besides the knowledge of business cultures and leadership styles in key Southeast Asian markets, the ASEAN Leadership Programme will also arm participants with the chance to go in-market to learn from as well as to network with both private and public sector leaders.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This not only helps our business leaders better navigate the region and capture the emerging trends, it extends the connections and growth into new markets.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We need employers, TACs, unions, PSEIs and training providers to all work closely together to empower our people.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On the individual level, we each has to take responsibility for our future by embracing lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Only then, can we capture new potential; only then, can we grow in step with the changes; and only then, can we rise to overcome the new demands of tomorrow.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It leaves me to thank Minister Lim Hng Kiang and let us congratulate him on the successful conclusion of the CPTPP or the TPP-11.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I also thank Minister Iswaran, Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling for their very comprehensive replies to our cuts.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I also want to thank all the Members who stayed till the end of the session, really testing the adjournment time limit.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
